options.title: Options
options.videoNote: Video settings apply when the game runs in its own window.
options.pressKey: {action}: press a key or button (Esc cancels)

door.libraryLocked: The library door is locked. The key must be somewhere in the house.
door.frontLocked: The storm is still raging outside. Nobody leaves tonight.
door.testLocked: Locked. The test key is in the box in the corner.

examine.hallBench: A bench for taking off muddy boots. Nobody has sat on it since the storm began.
examine.hallBear: A stuffed bear with glass eyes. It seems to follow you across the hall.
examine.reception: The guest book lies open. The last entry is smudged by rain.
examine.radio: Only static. The storm has taken the signal.
examine.libraryDesk: A tidy desk. One drawer is open and empty.
examine.wineRack: Dusty bottles, most of them older than the lodge's last owner.

library_key.name: Library key
library_key.description: A heavy brass key with a tag: LIBRARY.

room_c_key.name: Key of room C
room_c_key.description: A small silver key marked C.

lamp_oil.name: Lamp oil
lamp_oil.description: A bottle of lamp oil, still half full.

guest_ledger.name: Guest ledger
guest_ledger.description: Names and dates in a neat hand. One page has been torn out.
guest_ledger.read:
[b]Guest ledger, eight winters ago[/b]
Three railway clerks stayed that week: Pell on 3 March, Rudd on 4 March, Kerr on 5 March.
In the margin, in pencil: [c:#c8b890]stones moved - Rudd[/c].

torn_letter.name: Torn letter
torn_letter.description: A letter torn into four strips. The first line reads: Do not trust the owner.
torn_letter.read:
[b]Four strips[/b], in the order they came out of the box:
[c:#c8b890]{strips}[/c]

cellar_lantern.name: Cellar lantern
cellar_lantern.description: A hand lantern. It still holds a little light.

test_key.name: Test key
test_key.description: A key that only opens the test room.

fuse_wire.name: Fuse wire
fuse_wire.description: A short coil of thin fuse wire, kept in a drawer for a night like this.

fuse_cartridge.name: Fuse cartridge
fuse_cartridge.description: A porcelain fuse cartridge with the wire burnt through.

fuse_mended.name: Mended fuse
fuse_mended.description: The cartridge, rewired. It will carry the cellar circuit again.

view.hint: Drag to turn it. The + and - buttons, a pinch, R / V or the triggers zoom.

puzzle.again: There is nothing more to do here.

drawer.title: The locked drawer
drawer.intro: The lower drawer of the writing desk is shut with a brass lock of four wheels. Each wheel shows one digit.
drawer.wrong: The wheels turn, and nothing gives.
drawer.open: The lock clicks. In the drawer: a coil of fuse wire and a card in Emil's hand.
drawer.done: The drawer stands open. Nothing else is in it.
drawer.hint: Four digits. A date, perhaps: month and day.

timetable.title: The railway timetable
timetable.intro: The services of the pass are pinned up out of order. Put them in the order they run, the first of the morning at the top.
timetable.note1: The mail train is the first service of the day.
timetable.note2: The milk churns go on the train just before the goods wagons.
timetable.note3: The mountain coach runs after the goods train.
timetable.wrong: That cannot be right. One of the notes is broken.
timetable.solved: The timetable is clear: mail, milk, goods, coach.
timetable.done: You already know the order of the services.

letter.title: The torn letter
letter.intro: Four strips of one letter. Pick two strips to swap them until the sentences read in order.
letter.solved: The letter is whole. It was written to call Dr. Vale here.
letter.done: The letter is already pieced together.
letter.wrong: That does not read right yet.
letter.noItem: You have no torn letter to piece together.
letter.strip1: Do not trust the owner, Dr. Vale.
letter.strip2: Eight winters ago Emil Lindqvist moved the boundary stones at night,
letter.strip3: and what he buried that week is locked in his desk, under the date he chose.
letter.strip4: Ask who was in the house. Burn this. - A friend

fuse.title: The cellar fuse box
fuse.intro: The box stands open; its cartridge is gone. Four breakers wait under it, each marked with a service of the pass.
fuse.noFuse: You have no working fuse to fit.
fuse.fitted: The mended fuse clicks home. The breakers wait.
fuse.trip: The breakers fall back with a bang. Start again.
fuse.fixed: The lights come on, and far above the wind drops.
fuse.noPower: The lights are on. Nothing needs mending down here.

combo.fuse_mended: You wind the wire through the cartridge. It is a fuse again.
combo.refuse: Those two do not belong together.
combo.pick: Choose the item to combine with the {name}.

screens.noClues: No clues yet. Talk to the household and look around.
screens.hintItems: Tab or the shoulder buttons: next page.   Esc or B: close.
screens.hintBoard: Pick two clues to link them.   Z: undo   Y: redo   Esc or B: close.
screens.hintJournal: Tab, PageUp / PageDown or the shoulder buttons: change page.   Esc or B: close.

board.picked: Picked: {name}. Pick a second clue to link.
board.nothing: These two do not lead anywhere yet.
board.cannotRedo: The clues for that deduction are no longer known.

oil.title: Lantern and oil
oil.text: Dr. Vale took a lantern and lamp oil down to the cellar.

cellar.title: The long cellar
cellar.text: The cellar goes back further than its shelves.

page.title: The missing page
page.text: Dr. Vale came for a missing page of the survey.

argument.title: Supper quarrel
argument.text: Mara and Dr. Vale quarrelled at supper.

survey.title: The boundary stones
survey.text: The survey is about boundary stones, and page forty is the proof.

hedda.title: Hedda's letter
hedda.text: Hedda owns up to the torn letter.

adit.title: The adit
adit.text: Captain Haas admits an adit behind the third wine shelf.

ledger.title: Guest ledger
ledger.text: Three railway clerks stayed eight winters ago: Pell on 3 March, Rudd on 4 March, Kerr on 5 March. The margin says: stones moved - Rudd.

letter.title: Torn letter
letter.text: A letter torn into four strips, from room B.

letter_whole.title: The whole letter
letter_whole.text: Emil moved the stones at night, and what he buried is locked in his desk under the date he chose.

card.title: Fuse box card
card.text: Throw the breakers in the order of the day's services, first to last.

power.title: Power cut
power.text: The lights are out. The fuse box in the cellar needs a mended fuse.

d_date.title: The date he chose
d_date.text: Rudd's night was 4 March. The drawer code is 0403.

d_order.title: Breaker order
d_order.text: Throw the breakers in this order: mail, milk, goods, coach.

d_trail.title: Where Vale went
d_trail.text: Dr. Vale took light and oil into the long cellar.

d_motive.title: Why Vale came
d_motive.text: Vale came for the missing page, and Mara quarrelled with him about it.

d_author.title: Who wrote it
d_author.text: Hedda wrote the letter that called Dr. Vale to the lodge.

d_adit.title: The way down
d_adit.text: The adit behind the third wine shelf is where Vale went.

d_truth.title: The truth of it
d_truth.text: The stones were moved, the page proves it, and the household knew.

ch1_mara.greet: There you are. You must be the new night porter. Mara Lindqvist; the lodge is mine, and tonight's storm is nobody's fault.
ch1_mara.intro_c3: I will keep everyone safe tonight.
ch1_mara.intro: The pass closed at six. Until it opens we are six souls under this roof, and none of them in a good humour. Your work is the doors, the stove and the keys.
ch1_mara.tip: Walk the house. Look at what you like, pick up what you find, and do not wake the guests.
ch1_mara.worry: Wrong? A house full of strangers and a locked pass. That is the whole of it. Ask Hedda if you want more than that.
ch1_mara.promise: Safe. That is a good word to begin a shift with. Hold on to it.
ch1_mara.bye: Hedda is at the foot of the stairs, on the west side. Go and see her.
ch1_mara.again: Hedda is at the foot of the stairs. Go on.

ch1_hedda.greet: The porter. Good. I have been up since four and I have nothing to give you but trouble.
ch1_hedda.trouble: Dr. Vale, room C. He went up after supper. I took his hot water at ten and the door was locked; he did not answer. At midnight, the same.
ch1_hedda.asleep: A sleeper snores. I know a snore. There is no sound in that room at all.
ch1_hedda.nokey: The key to room C is the guest's own, and the spare hangs on Mrs. Lindqvist's ring. She will not lend it until she must.
ch1_hedda.seen: He quarrelled with Mara at supper. Afterwards he stood a long while by the cellar door. After that, nobody saw him.
ch1_hedda.conclude: A man has vanished from a locked house in a snowstorm. Find him, porter.

ch1_tobias.greet: The night porter? Come in, you look half frozen. There is soup on the back of the stove.
ch1_tobias.soup: Eight years I have cooked in this house and never seen the pass shut in November. Mind the pot, mind your feet.
ch1_tobias.busy: Later, then. The soup keeps. So does the storm.

ch1_haas.greet: Captain Haas, retired. Forty winters I guided people over that pass, and it still thinks it can surprise me.
ch1_haas.pass: It will not open before morning. Nobody who left tonight is coming back.
ch1_haas.who: Nobody could. That is the point of snow.
ch1_haas.wood: A man who brings wood is a man I will like.

ch1_lucian.greet: Lucian Arne, the Valley Courier. Please tell me the radio works.
ch1_lucian.hiss: Of course it does. I came up for a story about a land dispute and got a blizzard instead.
ch1_lucian.dispute: A story. Ask me tomorrow, when I am warm and you are less useful.

ch2_tobias.greet: You are asking about the doctor. Everybody is. Sit down; I sell nothing but facts.
ch2_tobias.fact_c2: Did you give them to him?
ch2_tobias.fact: He came into my kitchen at nine, polite as a bishop. He asked for a lantern and a can of lamp oil, and said his own lamp was giving trouble.
ch2_tobias.why: For the cellar. That is all he said. I thought he wanted to look over the wine.
ch2_tobias.gave: The oil, yes. One can. There is a second in the box by the door if you want it. The lantern I could not find; the house keeps its lanterns where it likes.
ch2_tobias.afraid: Afraid? No. Excited. Like a boy who has found the loose board in his father's attic.
ch2_tobias.close: That is all I know. The cellar, lamp oil, and a very happy man.
ch2_tobias.again: I have nothing to add. The cellar, lamp oil, a happy man. Ask somebody else.

ch2_haas.greet: Vale. A careful man. He measured the yard before breakfast and the cellar after lunch. A man measures what he does not trust.
ch2_haas.cellar: He asked me whether the cellar went back further than the shelves. I told him no. He wrote that down.
ch2_haas.deflect: A cellar goes as far as its walls. Do not bend your mind round it.
ch2_haas.thanks: That is kind of you. Remember you said it.
ch2_haas.warn: Everything hides something. That is what shelves are for.
ch2_haas.close: Look at the cellar yourself if you must. Mind the third shelf of the wine rack; the wood is rotten.
ch2_haas.again: I have said what I know. The third shelf is rotten. Leave it at that.

ch2_lucian.greet: Porter! Excellent. Vale's supper is still here, untouched. I find that eloquent.
ch2_lucian.page_c3: And what do you get out of it?
ch2_lucian.page: Between us: Vale surveys land for the railway company. A survey of this valley was filed here eight years ago, and the county copy is missing a page. Page forty. He came to find the original.
ch2_lucian.why: Page forty draws the line between this lodge and the railway's right of way. Move a line and you move a fortune.
ch2_lucian.who: Whoever gains from the line being where it is. A short list. It has one name and she owns the house.
ch2_lucian.you: A story. A good one. I am not ashamed of it.
ch2_lucian.close: Find Vale and you will find page forty, I would wager. Or the other way round.
ch2_lucian.again: I have told you what I know. Page forty. Go and find it.

ch2_mara.greet: You have spoken to Hedda, so you know Dr. Vale is gone.
ch2_mara.supper: We quarrelled at supper. I will not pretend otherwise; the whole table heard. He asked for the 1911 survey, I said the lodge's copy was lost, and he called me a liar in front of my cook.
ch2_mara.kind: It was. Thank you for noticing; most people notice the shouting.
ch2_mara.blunt: About the copy? I told him what I knew. My husband kept the papers and I never read them. I wish I had.
ch2_mara.accuse: I wanted him quiet. Not gone. Do not confuse the two, porter: one is a business and the other is a crime.
ch2_mara.close: Find him. Whatever he has found, I would rather it was found by someone I can talk to.
ch2_mara.again: Find him, porter. That is all I ask.

ch2_hedda.greet: I looked through the keyhole of room C. His bag is open on the chair and his bed is made.
ch2_hedda.think: A man who leaves his bag open means to come back. So where is he?
ch2_hedda.close: Ask the others. Somebody in this house knows more than they say.

ch3_hedda.greet: You are standing at room C. Do not tell me you want the key.
ch3_hedda.ask_c1: I found a torn letter in room B.
ch3_hedda.ask_c2: A man may be freezing in the dark.
ch3_hedda.ask_c3: Give me the key or I tell Mara you hid it.
ch3_hedda.ask: Mara gave me the spare at midnight and told me to keep it. I will hand it to whoever says the right thing.
ch3_hedda.letter: So Lucian kept it. I wrote that for the newspaper and for the doctor, two copies. Yes, I wrote 'do not trust the owner'. Is Mara kind to me? Always. Is she honest? Ask her about the boundary stones.
ch3_hedda.letter2: I did not mean any harm to come of it. I wanted a man with a measuring chain to ask the right question.
ch3_hedda.urgent: Yes. That is why I am still up. All right.
ch3_hedda.threat: Tell her. She knows I would never keep a key from a man who needed it. Here.
ch3_hedda.please: That is not good enough and not bad enough. Come back with a reason.
ch3_hedda.give: Take it. If he is in there, bring him to me.
ch3_hedda.again: You have the key. Use it.

ch3_tobias.greet: The doctor again? You have the face of a man who wants a key.
ch3_tobias.key_c1: You gave him lamp oil at nine. If he is hurt, the kitchen is part of it.
ch3_tobias.key_c2: I am the porter. I am owed the key.
ch3_tobias.key_c3: I will tell her it was my idea.
ch3_tobias.key: The spare of room C hangs in my pantry. Mrs. Lindqvist thinks I do not know. What do you offer me?
ch3_tobias.oil: Ha. You have been listening. Take it.
ch3_tobias.owed: Porter or bishop, you stand by my pot and not by my pantry. Ask somebody else.
ch3_tobias.idea: That would be generous and foolish. Take it.
ch3_tobias.give: It is on the hook behind the flour. Bring it back unbroken.
ch3_tobias.again: You have what you came for. Go on.

ch3_mara.greet: You found the library. I have not been in here since my husband's funeral.
ch3_mara.desk_c2: Tell me about the boundary stones.
ch3_mara.desk: This was Emil's desk. Ledgers, a letter opener, and a drawer I have never had the courage to open.
ch3_mara.fine: Not yet. Ask me a better question.
ch3_mara.ledger: That is his clerk's hand. Look: three men from the railway office stayed one night each, eight years ago. The first stayed three. Emil paid for that silence.
ch3_mara.stones: Emil moved two of them in the spring after the railway first came asking. He told me it was drainage. I believed him until Dr. Vale said 'right of way' at supper.
ch3_mara.confess: Page forty would show where the stones stood in 1911. If it shows what I fear, the lower field, the orchard and the road belong to the railway, and the Brandt farm was taken to make room for nothing.
ch3_mara.bye: Now you know what I could not say at supper. Find the doctor, and then find the page.
ch3_mara.again: I have told you everything I know. Find the doctor.

ch3_haas.greet_c1: May I search your room, Captain?
ch3_haas.greet: Porter. You go up and down these stairs like a man who has lost a button.
ch3_haas.room: Room D. The key is in my pocket. There is nothing there but old maps; take it if it settles your mind.
ch3_haas.gave: Do not thank me. A key is a small thing to lend a man who asks plainly.
ch3_haas.midnight: Here, at the east end, listening to the storm. A habit of old guides.
ch3_haas.nothing: Then go and do it somewhere else.

ch3_lucian.greet: Come in, come in. You have come about the stones; I can see it in your boots.
ch3_lucian.stones: Emil Lindqvist moved two boundary stones eight years ago, so the railway's right of way would bend round the lodge and through Brandt's farm. Vale suspected it. I can prove nothing without page forty.
ch3_lucian.print: If the page exists, I will. Whoever it hurts.
ch3_lucian.spare: Sparing is for people with other jobs.
ch3_lucian.again: Find the page, porter, and bring it to me before you bring it to anyone else.

ch4_haas.greet: Porter. You have read his sketch, then. Room C told you what I would not.
ch4_haas.greet_knows: Porter. Mara told you about the stones, and the sketch told you where to look. Then there is no sense in my silence.
ch4_haas.confess: Behind the third shelf is the old adit, the mine they cut before the lodge was built. Emil and I walled its mouth with a door and a latch eight years ago. I told Dr. Vale nothing. I thought it safer forgotten.
ch4_haas.why_c2: A man may be dying in there.
ch4_haas.why_c3: You could not have known he would go in.
ch4_haas.why: Say what you think of me. I have said worse.
ch4_haas.reason: Because Emil asked me, and Emil was my friend. Loyalty is a vice, but it is the only one I have kept.
ch4_haas.angry: Then open it. Quickly. Do not preach.
ch4_haas.calm: That is more than I deserve. Thank you.
ch4_haas.ready: You are back. The latch is waiting.
ch4_haas.plan: The latch falls from the dark side and cannot be lifted from there. A man needs a light and a lantern's worth of oil to go down and bring someone up.
ch4_haas.hint_lantern: Emil kept a lantern in a cardboard box in the nook, by the far wall. Go and get it.
ch4_haas.hint_power: The latch works from the cellar circuit, and the storm has killed the circuit. The fuse box is on the cellar wall. Emil kept wire in his library desk, and there is a spare cartridge in the other box in the kitchen corner. Then the order of the day's trains, if I remember how he set it.
ch4_haas.hint_oil: The cook keeps a can in the box by the kitchen door. Hurry.
ch4_haas.descend: The third shelf swings in on a rusted hinge and a breath of cold comes out of the dark. You light the lantern. The adit runs down, wet and low.
ch4_haas.found: Down here! Who is it? Bless you; I have run out of matches and of good sense.
ch4_haas.found2: The latch dropped behind me and I have been counting stones for six hours. Take this. Page forty, from the iron box under the first stone, exactly as the letter said.
ch4_haas.found4: Captain. I will forgive you when I am warm.
ch4_haas.up: You bring him up the steps into the lamplight. Outside, the wind has dropped. Dawn is not far.
ch4_haas.done: It is open and he is up. Go and see to him.

ch4_mara.greet_c1: I know about the stones, Mrs. Lindqvist.
ch4_mara.greet_c2: I think he is in the cellar.
ch4_mara.greet: You look like a man carrying something heavy. Is it about Vale?
ch4_mara.truth: Then you know why I could not say it. Say what you must, but find him first.
ch4_mara.cellar: The cellar? Emil never let me past the second shelf. The door is not locked. Go.
ch4_mara.bye: I will be here, by the fire.
ch4_mara.again: I will be here, by the fire.

ch4_hedda.confess: I wrote the letter. My father's farm went under the railway, and I wanted a man with a theodolite to ask a question.
ch4_hedda.sorry: I never meant to send him into the dark.
ch4_hedda.known: I did what I could, and it was not enough. Bring him back.

ch4_tobias.greet: If it is the cellar you are going to, you will want oil. There is a can in the box by the kitchen door.
ch4_tobias.bread: And take the heel of the loaf for the doctor. A man comes out of the dark hungry.

ch4_lucian.greet: I will keep Mara company in the hall. If you find the page, my pencil stays in my pocket until you say.
ch4_lucian.thanks: A promise. I have broken a few, but never one made to a man with a lantern.
ch4_lucian.later: Fair enough. I shall be around.
ch4_lucian.again: My pencil is in my pocket.

ch5_vale.greet: There he is, the man with the lantern. I owe you a bed, a breakfast and an explanation. First, the page.
ch5_vale.page: Page forty of the Ostrander survey, in the surveyor's own hand. The first stone stood at the foot of the cellar steps, not at the road.
ch5_vale.page2: Eight years ago Emil Lindqvist moved the road stone to bend the right of way round the lodge, and buried the proof in the adit.
ch5_vale.ask_c1: File it. The truth, all of it.
ch5_vale.ask_c2: Mara has lost enough tonight. Leave her the lodge.
ch5_vale.ask_c3: It was the Captain. He shut you in.
ch5_vale.ask: My report goes to the railway and the land office by noon, unless someone shows me a better way. What do you say, porter?
ch5_vale.wait: Take your time. The sun cannot hurry for us.
ch5_vale.done: Safe journey, porter. And thank you.
ch5_vale.truth_a: Then I file it as it is: the stones, the page, and Mrs. Lindqvist's honesty last night, which I will add in her favour.
ch5_vale.dawn_warm: By spring the Brandt land is back under the Brandt name. Mara keeps the house and sells the orchard to pay for it, and Hedda opens the first shutters of the year herself.
ch5_vale.dawn_cold: The report is filed. The lodge keeps its roof but loses the orchard and the road, and Mara speaks to nobody for a month. Hedda goes home to the Brandt land alone.
ch5_vale.dawn_end: You stand at the front door as the pass opens. It is the first morning in eight years without a lie in the house.
ch5_vale.bury_a: A page is only paper. If it burned in the lamp tonight, I could swear I never found it. Is that what you want?
ch5_vale.bury_b: The page curls and goes black in the lamp. You drop the guest ledger and the torn letter in after it, and the flame is a long time dying.
ch5_vale.bury_c: Vale files a report that calls the survey lost. Mara keeps the lodge. Hedda leaves at dawn and does not look back, and the porter keeps the keys and the silence.
ch5_vale.bury_end: Down in the cellar, behind the third shelf, a latch holds a little more firmly than before.
ch5_vale.accuse_a: The Captain? I heard no footsteps; the latch fell on its own. But he knew, and he said nothing. For a report, that is blame enough.
ch5_vale.accuse_b: I knew it would come to this. Go on, porter. Say it loud enough that the others hear.
ch5_vale.accuse_c: The Captain leaves on the first sledge down. Vale's report names an old man's silence and says nothing of the stones. Mara thanks you in a voice with no warmth in it.
ch5_vale.accuse_end: The lodge stands, the page goes back into a drawer, and winter closes over all of it.

ch5_mara.greet: He is safe. I do not know whether to thank you or to hate you for it.
ch5_mara.later: I will. If there is a lodge to thank you in.
ch5_mara.plan: Whatever the page says. I have been afraid of it for eight years, and there is relief in seeing it in lamplight.

ch5_hedda.greet: He is alive, then. I will leave at noon whatever is decided.
ch5_hedda.close: It was only ever that I wanted someone to look.

ch5_tobias.greet: Breakfast in ten minutes for anyone with a clear conscience, which is nobody. Eat anyway.

ch5_haas.greet: I will not argue with what you decide. I have been wrong for eight years.
ch5_haas.close: Whatever it costs me, it was cheaper than a man's life.

ch5_lucian.greet: Whatever you choose, remember that I was excellent company in a storm.
ch5_lucian.letter: That letter was Hedda's, you know. I would not print her name. I would print everything else.

1.title: The night shift
1.intro: Snow closed the pass at six. You have the keys, the stove and a house full of strangers until morning.

2.title: Cold supper
2.intro: Dr. Vale's supper is still on the table and nobody wants to say why he left it.

3.title: Room C
3.intro: A man's bag lies open behind a locked door. Whoever holds the key holds the first answer.

4.title: The old way
4.intro: Behind the third shelf of the wine rack the cellar goes further than anyone admitted.

5.title: Dawn
5.intro: The wind has dropped. The pass will open within the hour, and then everyone has a story to tell.

dawn.title: The Truth at Dawn
dawn.text: The truth is filed: the stones, the page and Mara's honesty. The Brandt land comes home, and the lodge learns to live without a lie.

quiet.title: The Quiet Way
quiet.text: The page burns and the lodge keeps its roof. Nobody is punished, and nobody is free of it.

long.title: The Long Winter
long.text: The Captain pays for a silence that was never only his. The lodge stands, and winter closes over everything.
